questions.question: Chip par 5 MΩ ka switched-capacitor resistor banana hai, switching frequency 20 kHz. Capacitor kitna lo, aur ΔV = 2 V par average current kitna hoga?
questions.explanation: R_eq = 1/(f·C) ⇒ C = 1/(2 × 10⁴ × 5 × 10⁶) = 10⁻¹¹ F = 10 pF. I = f·C·ΔV = 2 × 10⁴ × 10⁻¹¹ × 2 = 0.4 μA (check: 2 V/5 MΩ = 0.4 μA ✓). 1.59 pF tab aata hai jab 1/(2πfC) wala reactance formula laga dete ho — switching ke liye 2π nahi lagta. 4 μA me power-of-ten ki galti hai.

weeks.title: Binary numbers, audio file sizes and digital building blocks
weeks.summary: Is week aap binary aur decimal ke beech conversion, audio data rate aur WAV file size ka hisaab, analog vs digital computing ka trade-off, aur logic gates se adder jaise basic digital blocks seekhoge.
concepts: **Binary number system**: base 2, digits sirf 0 aur 1. Har position ka weight 2 ki power: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, .... Jaise 1011 = 8 + 0 + 2 + 1 = 11. N bits se 0 se 2ᴺ − 1 tak ke numbers ban sakte hain (8 bits ⇒ 0–255).

**Decimal → binary**: baar-baar 2 se divide karo aur remainders likho; answer remainders ko **neeche se upar** padhne par milta hai. Ya phir sabse badi 2 ki power ghatao (38 = 32 + 4 + 2 ⇒ 100110). Hex (base 16) me 4 bits = 1 hex digit, jaise 1111 = F.

**Bits aur bytes**: 1 byte = 8 bits. Data rate aksar bits per second (bit/s) me, file size bytes me. Yahan 1 kB = 1000 bytes aur 1 MB = 10⁶ bytes le rahe hain (computers kabhi-kabhi 1024 bhi use karte hain).

**Audio data rate**: uncompressed (PCM/WAV) audio ka bit rate = sampling rate × bits per sample × channels. File size (bytes) = bit rate × duration ÷ 8, plus ek chhota header (WAV me ~44 bytes). MP3 jaise formats compression se size ~10× kam karte hain.

**Analog vs digital computing**: analog computer (op-amp adders, integrators) continuous voltages par seedha maths karta hai — fast aur kam power, par noise, drift aur component tolerance se accuracy limited. Digital computer numbers ko bits me rakhta hai — har stage par signal 0/1 me restore hota hai, isliye noise jama nahi hota aur precision bits badha kar badhayi ja sakti hai.

**Digital building blocks**: logic gates (NOT, AND, OR, XOR) se sab kuch banta hai. **Half adder**: Sum = A XOR B, Carry = A AND B. Full adder teen bits (A, B, carry-in) jodta hai; N full adders chain karke N-bit adder. Flip-flops/registers bits store karte hain, multiplexer kai inputs me se ek chunta hai.

example.problem: 3 minute ka stereo gaana 44.1 kHz par 16-bit samples me WAV file me save kiya. File size kitna hoga (header ignore karo, 1 MB = 10⁶ bytes)?
steps: Bytes per second = 1,411,200 ÷ 8 = 176,400 B/s.
Duration = 3 × 60 = 180 s.
Answer: **≈ 31.8 MB** (isi gaane ki 128 kbit/s MP3 sirf ~2.9 MB hoti).

mistakes: Division method me remainders ko upar se neeche padh lena. Pehla remainder sabse kam weight (LSB) ka hota hai, isliye neeche se upar padho.
bits ko bytes samajh lena. File size bytes me chahiye to 8 se divide karna mat bhoolo.
Stereo me channels = 2 bhool jaana. Mono ka size stereo ka aadha hota hai.
revision: Decimal → binary: ÷2 karo, remainders neeche se upar.
Bit rate = fs × bits × channels; bytes = bits ÷ 8.
Half adder: Sum = XOR, Carry = AND.
Digital: noise har stage par restore; analog: fast par noise jama hota hai.

questions.question: Decimal 38 ko binary me likho.
questions.explanation: 38 = 32 + 4 + 2 ⇒ 100110. Division se: remainders 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 1 aate hain; neeche se upar padho to 100110. 011001 tab aata hai jab remainders upar se neeche padh lete ho — wo 25 hai.

questions.question: Binary 11010 ka decimal value kya hai?
questions.explanation: Weights 16, 8, 4, 2, 1: 16 + 8 + 0 + 2 + 0 = 26. 11 tab aata hai jab bits ko ulta (01011) padh lete ho, aur 13 ya 52 tab jab weights ek position khisak jaate hain.

questions.question: Landline jaisi digital voice: mono, 8 kHz sampling, 8 bits per sample. Bit rate kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Bit rate = 8000 × 8 × 1 = 64,000 bit/s = 64 kbit/s. 64 kbyte/s me bits aur bytes mix ho gaye (asli me 8 kbyte/s), aur 128 kbit/s stereo maan lene se aata hai.

questions.question: 1 minute ki stereo recording 48 kHz par 24-bit samples me hai. Uncompressed size kitna hai (1 MB = 10⁶ bytes, header ignore)?
questions.explanation: Bits = 48000 × 24 × 2 × 60 = 138,240,000. Bytes = ÷8 = 17,280,000 = 17.28 MB. 138.24 MB tab aata hai jab bits ko bytes me nahi badalte, 8.64 MB mono maan lene se, aur 0.288 MB sirf 1 second ka size hai.

questions.question: Half adder ke inputs A = 1 aur B = 1 hain. Outputs kya honge?
questions.explanation: Sum = A XOR B = 1 XOR 1 = 0, Carry = A AND B = 1. Binary me 1 + 1 = 10, yaani sum bit 0 aur carry 1. 'Sum = 1, Carry = 1' tab aata hai jab Sum ko OR samajh lete ho.

questions.question: Ek voice recorder me 10 MB (10 × 10⁶ bytes) memory hai. Wo mono audio 16 kHz par 12-bit samples me record karta hai (samples bina gap ke pack hote hain). Lagbhag kitne second ki recording aayegi?
questions.explanation: Memory = 10 × 10⁶ × 8 = 8 × 10⁷ bits. Bit rate = 16000 × 12 = 192,000 bit/s. Time = 8 × 10⁷ / 192,000 ≈ 417 s (≈ 7 min). 52 s tab aata hai jab bytes ko bits me badalna (×8) bhool jaate ho, 313 s jab har sample ko 16 bits me store maan lete ho, aur 208 s jab stereo maan lete ho.

questions.question: Binary 10101111 ko hexadecimal me likho.
questions.explanation: 4-4 bits ke group banao: 1010 = A, 1111 = F, to AF. FA tab aata hai jab groups ka order ulta kar dete ho, aur 175 iska decimal value hai, hex nahi.

questions.question: Ek voice stream 64 kbit/s par chal rahi hai. Ye kitne kB per second hai (1 kB = 1000 bytes)?
questions.explanation: 1 byte = 8 bits, to 64 kbit/s ÷ 8 = 8 kB/s. 64 kB/s bits ko bytes samajhna hai, aur 512 kB/s tab aata hai jab 8 se divide ki jagah multiply kar dete ho.

questions.question: Kaunsa logic gate output 1 tabhi deta hai jab uske do inputs alag-alag hon?
questions.explanation: XOR: 0,1 aur 1,0 par 1; 0,0 aur 1,1 par 0. Isi liye half adder ka Sum = A XOR B hai. OR 1,1 par bhi 1 deta hai, aur AND sirf 1,1 par 1 deta hai.

questions.question: Decimal 100 ko binary me likho.
questions.explanation: 100 = 64 + 32 + 4, to 1100100. Division method: remainders 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 1, 1 aate hain, jinhe neeche se upar padhna hai. 0010011 tab aata hai jab remainders ko upar se neeche padh lete ho.

questions.question: 4 minute ka gaana 128 kbit/s MP3 me hai. File size kitna hoga (1 MB = 10⁶ bytes)?
questions.explanation: Bits = 128000 × 240 s = 30,720,000. Bytes = ÷ 8 = 3,840,000 = 3.84 MB. 30.72 MB tab aata hai jab 8 se divide karna bhool jaate ho, 0.064 MB tab jab minutes ko seconds me nahi badalte, aur 7.68 MB tab jab stereo ke liye 2 se multiply kar dete ho — MP3 bit rate me dono channels pehle se shaamil hain.

questions.question: Ek 4-bit adder (full adders ki chain) me 1011 aur 0110 jode gaye. Carry-out ko bhi milakar result kya hai?
questions.explanation: 1011 = 11, 0110 = 6, sum = 17 = 10001 (carry-out 1, baaki bits 0001). 1101 tab aata hai jab har bit par sirf XOR karte ho aur carries bhool jaate ho, aur 0001 me 4 bits ke bahar wala carry-out chhoot gaya.

questions.question: Phone me 32 GB (32 × 10⁹ bytes) free hai. Uncompressed audio 48 kHz, 16-bit, stereo me record karna hai. Lagbhag kitne ghante ki recording ho sakti hai?
questions.explanation: Bytes per second = 48000 × 2 bytes × 2 channels = 192,000 B/s. Time = 32 × 10⁹ / 192,000 ≈ 166,667 s ≈ 46 h. 93 h mono ka answer hai (channels = 2 bhool gaye), 370 h tab aata hai jab memory ko bits me le lete ho, aur 5.8 h tab jab bit rate ko bytes per second maan lete ho (8 se divide bhool kar).

questions.question: CD-quality WAV (44.1 kHz, 16-bit, stereo) ko 192 kbit/s MP3 me badla. Compression ratio kitna hai, aur 5 minute ke gaane ki MP3 kitni badi hogi (1 MB = 10⁶ bytes)?
questions.explanation: WAV bit rate = 44100 × 16 × 2 = 1,411,200 bit/s. Ratio = 1411.2/192 ≈ 7.35. MP3 size = 192000 × 300 / 8 = 7,200,000 bytes = 7.2 MB. 3.68× tab aata hai jab WAV ko mono le lete ho, 57.6 MB tab jab 8 se divide bhool jaate ho, aur 58.8× tab jab ek rate bits me aur doosra bytes me le kar compare karte ho.

questions.question: Decimal 200 ko binary aur hexadecimal dono me likho.
questions.explanation: 200 = 128 + 64 + 8, to binary 11001000. Hex ke liye 4-4 bits: 1100 = C, 1000 = 8, to C8. 00010011 tab aata hai jab division ke remainders upar se neeche padh lete ho, aur 8C me nibbles ka order ulta ho gaya.

weeks.title: Sending signals: cables, radio waves and modulation
weeks.summary: Is week aap wired links me delay, reflection aur ringing, radio waves ki wavelength aur antenna size, aur AM/FM modulation kyun aur kaise hota hai — ye sab simple numbers ke saath seekhoge.
concepts: **Wired link me delay**: cable me signal light ki speed se thoda dheere chalta hai, lagbhag v ≈ 2 × 10⁸ m/s (c ka ~2/3). 1 m cable ≈ 5 ns delay. Jab cable itni lambi ho ki ye delay signal ke rise time ke barabar ya zyada ho, to cable ko simple wire nahi maan sakte.

**Reflection aur termination**: har cable ka ek characteristic impedance Z0 hota hai (coax 50 Ω ya 75 Ω). Agar far end par load Z0 ke barabar na ho (jaise open end), to signal wapas reflect hota hai aur 2 × (length/v) baad sender par echo pahunchta hai. Matching resistor (= Z0) lagane se reflection khatam.

**Ringing**: reflections ya wires ka parasitic L aur C mil kar step ke baad oscillation (ringing) banate hain, jiski frequency ≈ 1/(2π√(LC)). Isse digital signals galat padhe ja sakte hain; termination aur chhote traces se ise kam karte hain.

**Radio waves**: EM waves free space me c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s par chalti hain. **Wavelength λ = c/f**. Achhi antenna ki length λ ke order ki hoti hai — common choice λ/4 (monopole) ya λ/2 (dipole). 100 MHz ⇒ λ = 3 m, quarter-wave 75 cm.

**Modulation kyun**: audio (20 Hz–20 kHz) ko seedha bhejne ke liye km-lambi antenna chahiye, aur sab stations ek hi band me takra jaayenge. Isliye audio ko ek high-frequency **carrier** par chadhaate hain: antenna chhoti, aur har station alag carrier frequency par.

**AM**: carrier ka amplitude audio ke hisaab se badalta hai. Single tone fm se carrier fc ke saath sidebands fc ± fm bante hain, bandwidth = 2fm. **Modulation index** m = (Vmax − Vmin)/(Vmax + Vmin) envelope se; m ≤ 1 rakho warna distortion.

**FM**: carrier ki frequency audio ke hisaab se badalti hai (peak deviation Δf). Bandwidth (Carson's rule) ≈ 2(Δf + fm). FM zyada bandwidth leta hai par amplitude noise se kam affect hota hai, isliye music ke liye better. India me AM medium wave ~0.5–1.7 MHz, FM 88–108 MHz.

example.problem: 5 kHz audio ko seedha radio wave bana kar bhejna ho to quarter-wave antenna kitni lambi chahiye? Usi audio ko 100 MHz FM carrier par bhejo to?
steps: Quarter-wave = 60/4 = 15 km — bilkul impractical.
100 MHz par λ = 3 × 10⁸ / 10⁸ = 3 m.
Quarter-wave = 3/4 = 0.75 m = 75 cm — car ya radio par aaraam se lag jaati hai.
Answer: **15 km vs 75 cm** — isi liye modulation zaroori hai.

mistakes: λ = c/f me MHz/GHz ko Hz me badalna bhool jaana. 2.4 GHz = 2.4 × 10⁹ Hz.
Cable reflection ka time nikaalte waqt sirf one-way delay le lena. Echo ko jaana aur wapas aana dono padta hai, yaani 2 × length/v.
AM ki bandwidth fm maan lena. Dono sidebands hote hain, isliye bandwidth 2fm hai.
revision: AM: sidebands fc ± fm, BW = 2fm, m = (Vmax − Vmin)/(Vmax + Vmin).

questions.question: 2.4 GHz WiFi signal ki free-space wavelength kitni hai?
questions.explanation: λ = c/f = 3 × 10⁸ / 2.4 × 10⁹ = 0.125 m = 12.5 cm. GHz ko 10⁹ ki jagah 10⁸ ya 10¹⁰ le lene par 1.25 m ya 1.25 cm aata hai — power of 10 dhyaan se.

questions.question: 1 MHz ke AM carrier ko ek single 5 kHz tone se modulate kiya. Output me kaunsi frequencies hongi?
questions.explanation: AM me carrier fc ke saath sidebands fc ± fm aate hain: 1000 ± 5 = 995 aur 1005 kHz. Bandwidth = 2 × 5 = 10 kHz. 990/1010 kHz tab aata hai jab sidebands ko fc ± 2fm samajh lete ho (bandwidth ko ek side ka offset maan kar).

questions.question: 900 MHz mobile band ke liye quarter-wave antenna ki length lagbhag kitni hogi?
questions.explanation: λ = 3 × 10⁸ / 9 × 10⁸ = 0.333 m = 33.3 cm. Quarter-wave = 33.3/4 ≈ 8.3 cm. 33.3 cm poori wavelength hai aur 16.7 cm half-wave — quarter lena bhool gaye.

questions.question: Oscilloscope par AM signal ka envelope maximum 12 V aur minimum 4 V (peak) tak jaata hai. Modulation index m kitna hai?
questions.explanation: m = (Vmax − Vmin)/(Vmax + Vmin) = (12 − 4)/(12 + 4) = 8/16 = 0.5. 0.33 = 4/12 seedha ratio hai, aur 0.67 = 8/12 me denominator galat hai.

questions.question: 20 m lambi cable ka far end open hai, aur cable me signal speed 2 × 10⁸ m/s hai. Sender par bheja gaya pulse reflect hokar kitne time baad wapas aayega?
questions.explanation: Pulse ko 20 m jaana aur 20 m wapas aana hai: 40 m / (2 × 10⁸ m/s) = 2 × 10⁻⁷ s = 200 ns. 100 ns sirf one-way delay hai, aur 133 ns tab aata hai jab cable me bhi light ki speed 3 × 10⁸ m/s le lete ho.

questions.question: Ek FM station 98.3 MHz par hai, peak deviation Δf = 75 kHz aur highest audio frequency fm = 15 kHz. Carson's rule se bandwidth aur quarter-wave antenna ki length kya hai?
questions.explanation: Bandwidth ≈ 2(Δf + fm) = 2(75 + 15) = 180 kHz. λ = 3 × 10⁸ / 98.3 × 10⁶ ≈ 3.05 m, quarter-wave ≈ 0.76 m = 76 cm. 30 kHz AM wala formula (2fm) hai, aur 3.05 m poori wavelength hai.

questions.question: Ek 10 m lambi cable me signal 2 × 10⁸ m/s se chalta hai. One-way delay kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Delay = 10 / (2 × 10⁸) = 5 × 10⁻⁸ s = 50 ns (yaani ~5 ns per metre). 33 ns tab aata hai jab light ki free-space speed c le lete ho, aur 100 ns echo ka round-trip time hai, one-way nahi.

questions.question: India me FM radio broadcast kis frequency band me hota hai?
questions.explanation: FM broadcast 88–108 MHz me hai. 0.5–1.7 MHz AM medium wave ka band hai, 2.4 GHz WiFi ka, aur 20 Hz–20 kHz khud audio ki range hai jo carrier par chadhaayi jaati hai.

questions.question: Ek AM station 4 kHz tak ka audio bhejta hai. Uski bandwidth kitni hai?
questions.explanation: AM me carrier ke dono taraf sidebands bante hain (fc ± fm), to bandwidth = 2fm = 2 × 4 = 8 kHz. 4 kHz tab aata hai jab sirf ek sideband ginte ho.

questions.question: 150 MHz ke liye half-wave (λ/2) dipole antenna ki length kitni hogi?
questions.explanation: λ = 3 × 10⁸ / 1.5 × 10⁸ = 2 m, to λ/2 = 1 m. 2 m poori wavelength hai, aur 50 cm quarter-wave (λ/4) hai — dipole ke liye λ/2 chahiye.

questions.question: Ek AM signal ke envelope ka maximum 10 V hai aur modulation index m = 0.6 hai. Envelope ka minimum kitna hoga?
questions.explanation: m = (Vmax − Vmin)/(Vmax + Vmin) ⇒ 0.6(10 + Vmin) = 10 − Vmin ⇒ 6 + 0.6Vmin = 10 − Vmin ⇒ 1.6Vmin = 4 ⇒ Vmin = 2.5 V. 4 V tab aata hai jab Vmin = Vmax(1 − m) le lete ho, aur 6 V tab jab m × Vmax ko hi minimum maan lete ho.

questions.question: Ek PCB trace ka parasitic inductance 10 nH aur capacitance 10 pF hai. Step ke baad ringing frequency lagbhag kitni hogi?
questions.explanation: LC = 10⁻⁸ × 10⁻¹¹ = 10⁻¹⁹, √(LC) ≈ 3.16 × 10⁻¹⁰ s. f = 1/(2π × 3.16 × 10⁻¹⁰) ≈ 5.03 × 10⁸ Hz ≈ 503 MHz (period ~2 ns). 3.16 GHz tab aata hai jab 2π bhool jaate ho; 50.3 MHz aur 5.03 GHz nano/pico prefixes ki power-of-ten galtiyan hain.

questions.question: Ek lambi cable me kahin fault (open) hai. Sender par bheja gaya pulse 300 ns baad echo ban kar wapas aaya. Cable me signal speed 2 × 10⁸ m/s hai. Fault sender se kitni door hai?
questions.explanation: Echo jaata aur wapas aata hai: 2d = v·t = 2 × 10⁸ × 300 × 10⁻⁹ = 60 m, to d = 30 m. 60 m tab aata hai jab 2 se divide karna bhool jaate ho, aur 45 m tab jab cable ki speed ki jagah c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s le lete ho.

questions.question: Ek FM channel me peak deviation Δf = 50 kHz aur highest audio fm = 10 kHz hai. Carson's rule se iski bandwidth kitni hai, aur utni bandwidth me usi 10 kHz audio wale kitne AM channels aa sakte hain?
questions.explanation: FM: 2(Δf + fm) = 2(50 + 10) = 120 kHz. Har AM channel = 2fm = 20 kHz, to 120/20 = 6 channels. 12 channels tab aata hai jab AM bandwidth fm (10 kHz) maan lete ho, 100 kHz me fm bhool gaye, aur 60 kHz me 2 ka factor chhoot gaya.

questions.question: Ek digital signal ka rise time 2 ns hai, aur PCB par signal 1.5 × 10⁸ m/s se chalta hai. Trace ko kitni length par "simple wire" maanna band kar dena chahiye (jab one-way delay rise time ke barabar ho jaaye)?
questions.explanation: Length = v × t = 1.5 × 10⁸ × 2 × 10⁻⁹ = 0.3 m = 30 cm. Isse lambe trace par reflections aur ringing ka dhyaan rakhna padta hai. 60 cm tab aata hai jab PCB speed ki jagah c le lete ho, 15 cm tab jab round-trip ko rise time ke barabar rakhte ho, aur 3 m power-of-ten ki galti hai.

weeks.title: Capacitor energy puzzles and course recap
weeks.summary: Is aakhri week me aap capacitor energy, current source se capacitor charging, RC charging me hone wala energy loss, charge sharing aur stepwise charging jaise mixed problems solve karoge, aur poore course ka recap karoge.
concepts: **Capacitor energy**: E = ½CV² = Q²/(2C). Voltage double ⇒ energy 4 guna. Supercapacitor (jaise 10 F, 2.7 V) bhi sirf ~36 J store karta hai, jabki phone battery (~15 Wh) ~54,000 J — isliye supercaps fast burst ke liye, bulk storage ke liye nahi.

**Current source se charging**: constant I se capacitor charge karo to dV/dt = I/C, yaani voltage seedhi line (ramp) me badhta hai: V(t) = V0 + I·t/C. Ye ADC ke ramp generators aur timers me use hota hai.

**RC charging ka energy loss**: 0 V capacitor ko R ke through Vs se full charge karo. Source deta hai Q·Vs = CVs², capacitor store karta hai ½CVs², aur baaki **½CVs² resistor me heat** — R chahe kitna bhi ho! R sirf time (τ) badalta hai, loss nahi.

**Stepwise charging**: agar Vs ko N barabar steps me badhao (har step par capacitor ko settle hone do), to har step me loss ½C(Vs/N)², total = ½CVs²/N. Jitne zyada steps, utna kam loss — energy-efficient circuits (adiabatic charging) ka idea yahi hai.

**Charge sharing loss**: do capacitors jodne par charge conserve hota hai par energy ghatti hai. Do barabar capacitors (ek V par, ek 0 par) jodo to final V/2 aur aadhi energy heat ban jaati hai, connecting wire ka resistance chahe kitna bhi chhota ho.

**Course recap**: gadget ko blocks me dekho (week 1) → circuit laws aur analysis (weeks 2, 4, 5, 8) → time-varying signals aur RC (weeks 3, 6, 7) → digital duniya (weeks 9, 10) → communication (week 11). Har problem me units, sign convention aur sanity check se answer verify karo.

example.problem: 2 mA constant current source ek 100 μF capacitor (shuru me 0 V) ko charge karta hai. 5 V tak pahunchne me kitna time lagega, aur tab capacitor me kitni energy hogi?
steps: Time to 5 V = 5/20 = 0.25 s.
Charge check: Q = I·t = 2 × 10⁻³ × 0.25 = 0.5 mC = C·V = 100 μF × 5 V ✓.
Energy = ½CV² = ½ × 100 × 10⁻⁶ × 25 = 1.25 mJ.

mistakes: Socha ki chhota R lagane se charging ka energy loss kam hoga. Ek step me charging ka loss hamesha ½CVs² hai, R se independent.
Charge sharing me energy conservation laga dena. Charge conserve karo (Q = CV), phir energy alag se nikaalo.
½CV² me ½ bhool jaana, ya μF/mJ ke prefixes mix karna.
revision: RC charging: source CV², capacitor ½CV², resistor ½CV².
N steps me charging: loss = ½CV²/N.
Equal caps sharing (V aur 0): final V/2, aadhi energy loss.

questions.question: 1 F ka supercapacitor 5 V tak charged hai. Usme kitni energy store hai?
questions.explanation: E = ½CV² = ½ × 1 × 25 = 12.5 J. 25 J ½ bhoolne se aata hai, aur 5 J = C × V (wo charge Q = 5 C hai, energy nahi).

questions.question: 1 mA ka constant current source 10 μF capacitor (shuru me 0 V) ko 20 ms tak charge karta hai. Capacitor ka voltage kitna hoga?
questions.explanation: V = I·t/C = 10⁻³ × 20 × 10⁻³ / 10 × 10⁻⁶ = 2 × 10⁻⁵ / 10⁻⁵ = 2 V. 0.2 V ya 20 V ms aur μF ke prefixes me ek galti se aate hain.

questions.question: 0 V wala 100 μF capacitor 1 kΩ resistor ke through 10 V DC source se poora charge kiya gaya. Is process me resistor me kitni energy heat bani?
questions.explanation: Source ne diya Q·V = CV² = 100 × 10⁻⁶ × 100 = 10 mJ. Capacitor me store hua ½CV² = 5 mJ. Baaki 10 − 5 = 5 mJ resistor me heat. 10 mJ source ki total energy hai, aur 0 mJ tab lagta hai jab sochte ho ki saari energy capacitor me chali gayi.

questions.question: 10 μF capacitor 8 V par charged hai. Use ek uncharged 10 μF capacitor se jod diya. Is process me kitni energy lose (heat) hui?
questions.explanation: Pehle: ½ × 10 μF × 64 = 320 μJ. Charge 80 μC, total C = 20 μF, final V = 4 V. Baad me: ½ × 20 μF × 16 = 160 μJ. Loss = 320 − 160 = 160 μJ. 0 μJ energy conserve maan lene ka trap hai, aur 320 μJ shuru ki poori energy.

questions.question: Back-of-the-envelope: ek phone battery 15 Wh store karti hai. Utni energy store karne ke liye 10 F, 2.7 V ke kitne supercapacitors (full charged) chahiye honge?
questions.explanation: 15 Wh = 15 × 3600 = 54,000 J. Ek supercap: ½ × 10 × 2.7² ≈ 36.5 J. N ≈ 54,000/36.5 ≈ 1480 ≈ 1500. 150 tab aata hai jab Wh ko J me badalte waqt 3600 ki jagah 360 le lete ho. Isse samajh aata hai ki supercaps bulk energy ke liye kyun nahi hain.

questions.question: 100 μF capacitor (0 V) ko resistor ke through 10 V tak charge karna hai, par do steps me: pehle source 5 V (poora settle hone do), phir source 10 V. Dono steps me resistor me total kitni energy heat bani?
questions.explanation: Har step me voltage jump 5 V hai, aur ek step ka loss = ½C(ΔV)² = ½ × 100 × 10⁻⁶ × 25 = 1.25 mJ. Do steps: 2 × 1.25 = 2.5 mJ. Ek hi step (0 → 10 V) me loss 5 mJ hota — steps se loss aadha ho gaya. 1.25 mJ sirf ek step ka loss hai.

questions.question: 100 μF capacitor me 2 mC charge store hai. Usme kitni energy hai?
questions.explanation: E = Q²/(2C) = (2 × 10⁻³)² / (2 × 10⁻⁴) = 4 × 10⁻⁶ / 2 × 10⁻⁴ = 0.02 J = 20 mJ. (Check: V = Q/C = 20 V, ½CV² = ½ × 10⁻⁴ × 400 = 20 mJ ✓.) 40 mJ me 2 bhool gaye, aur 0.02 mJ J ko mJ me badalne ki galti hai.

questions.question: Ek capacitor ka voltage double kar diya. Uski stored energy par kya asar hoga?
questions.explanation: E = ½CV², to V double ⇒ V² 4 guna ⇒ energy 4 guna. 2 guna charge (Q = CV) ke liye sach hai, energy ke liye nahi.

questions.question: 0 V capacitor ko ek hi step me Vs se resistor ke through full charge kiya jaata hai. Resistor 1 kΩ se badal kar 100 Ω kar diya. Resistor me heat bani energy par kya asar hoga?
options: Koi asar nahi, ½CVs² hi rahegi
questions.explanation: Ek step ki charging me resistor me heat hamesha ½CVs² hoti hai, R kitna bhi ho. Chhota R sirf charging fast karta hai (τ = RC chhota), par peak current bada ho jaata hai, aur total loss wahi rehta hai. Chhota R matlab kam loss — ye is topic ki classic galti hai.

questions.question: 200 μF capacitor shuru me 1 V par hai. 4 mA ka constant current source use 0.5 s tak charge karta hai. Ab capacitor ka voltage kitna hai?
questions.explanation: ΔV = I·t/C = 4 × 10⁻³ × 0.5 / (200 × 10⁻⁶) = 10 V. V = V0 + ΔV = 1 + 10 = 11 V. 10 V tab aata hai jab shuru ka 1 V bhool jaate ho, aur 1.01 V me mA ya μF ka prefix galat lag gaya.

questions.question: 200 μF capacitor (0 V) ko 8 V tak charge karna hai, par 4 barabar steps me (2, 4, 6, 8 V; har step par settle hone do). Resistor me total kitni energy heat banegi?
questions.explanation: Har step ka loss = ½C(2 V)² = ½ × 200 × 10⁻⁶ × 4 = 0.4 mJ. 4 steps me 1.6 mJ (= ½CVs²/N = 6.4/4). 6.4 mJ ek step wala loss hai, 0.4 mJ sirf ek step ka hai, aur 3.2 mJ tab aata hai jab steps se loss sirf aadha maan lete ho.

questions.question: 2 μF capacitor 10 V par aur 3 μF capacitor 5 V par charged hain. Unke + terminals aapas me aur − terminals aapas me jod diye. Final voltage aur heat me gayi energy kitni hai?
questions.explanation: Q = 2 × 10 + 3 × 5 = 35 μC, V = 35/5 = 7 V. Energy pehle = ½ × 2 × 100 + ½ × 3 × 25 = 100 + 37.5 = 137.5 μJ, baad me ½ × 5 × 49 = 122.5 μJ. Loss = 15 μJ. 7.5 V voltages ka simple average hai (capacitances barabar nahi hain), 0 μJ energy conserve maanna hai, aur 122.5 μJ final energy hai, loss nahi.

questions.question: 10 F ka supercapacitor 2.7 V par full charged hai. Ek burst load use 1.35 V tak discharge karta hai. Load ko kitni energy mili?
questions.explanation: E_pehle = ½ × 10 × 2.7² ≈ 36.45 J, E_baad = ½ × 10 × 1.35² ≈ 9.11 J. Mili = 36.45 − 9.11 ≈ 27.3 J — voltage aadha hone par bhi 75% energy nikal gayi. 9.1 J tab aata hai jab ½C(ΔV)² le lete ho, 18.2 J tab jab sochte ho ki aadha voltage = aadhi energy, aur 36.5 J poori energy hai.

questions.question: Ek ideal 2 mA constant current source seedha ek 50 μF capacitor (0 V) ko 0.1 s tak charge karta hai (beech me koi resistor nahi). Source ne kitni energy di, aur kitni heat bani?
questions.explanation: Q = I·t = 0.2 mC, V = Q/C = 4 V, capacitor energy = ½ × 50 × 10⁻⁶ × 16 = 0.4 mJ. Current source ka voltage capacitor ke saath 0 se 4 V tak ramp karta hai (average 2 V), to source energy = 0.2 mC × 2 V = 0.4 mJ — sab capacitor me, heat zero. 0.8 mJ = Q × 4 V tab aata hai jab source ko fixed 4 V wala voltage source maan lete ho; ½ loss wala rule sirf fixed voltage se ek step charging par lagta hai.

questions.question: 0 V wala 50 μF capacitor 2 kΩ ke through 10 V DC se charge hota hai. Full charge tak source ne total kitni energy di, aur ~99% charge hone me lagbhag kitna time laga?
questions.explanation: Source energy = Q·Vs = CVs² = 50 × 10⁻⁶ × 100 = 5 mJ (aadha 2.5 mJ capacitor me, aadha resistor me heat). τ = 2000 × 50 × 10⁻⁶ = 0.1 s, aur ~99% ke liye 5τ = 0.5 s. 2.5 mJ sirf capacitor ki energy hai, aur 0.1 s sirf ek τ hai (tab sirf 63% charge).
